In Praise of Portables

1/3

these Portables are a good "middle of the road," with LLM knowledge (aka 30-second knowledge) on one side and deep diving an oeuvre on the other

fwiw they are not very Portable lol, they are 800 pages, they take time

but u are gonna understand a man's worldview and major works once ur done...u get a solid intro/ongoing footnotes from a scholar or professor, lovingly crafted, they tend to be a thoughtful blend of primary and secondary material

and u will see time and time again that the LLM synopsis does not capture the essence of what these books show u. 

2/3

if you grasp 75% of it, that's $$. its okay if some goes over ur head.

you wont be smartest guy in the room, but u are conversant/familiar, and will slowly build a rolodex of great thinker worldviews.

without exception, someone who has been tagged as "great thinker" for the past 250-500+ years, they've earned it, u will see why. impossible to glean from 30-second LLM "gimme the skinny." 

also, each Portable is prob $5.99 in "very good condition" on most thrift sites...$50-60 puts u in real good position.

dont be the "LLM-level" guy, u only sound smart against other LLM-level guys, eventually u will bump into someone who knows their shit and they'll silently write u off/tag u with the "talks a lot without knowing what he's talking abt." Book LARP, I guess u could say. 

3/3

do the heavy lifting. most didn't to begin with, and in LLM-Land it'll only get worse.

personal favs from these, both Emerson and Samuel Johnson are eminently readable...just mind-bogglingly gifted writers, masters of the craft.

turn the twtr off this wknd, there aint shit on here except guys victory-lapping NVDA puts that just rallied from $2 to $4 (with a cost basis of $84.50)
